correctness.rationale: For each three-space \(U\), its seventh-power sum equals the nonzero 3x3 Moore determinant of any binary basis. Scalar multiplication sends the value to \(\\(\lambda^7\)\) times itself, so the subgroup \(H\) of seventh powers has size 9. Exactly the nine subfield three-spaces form an exceptional orbit; all 1386 remaining spaces form 22 scalar orbits. A complete finite classification distributes those free orbits 4 above \(H\) and 3 above each other coset; each contributes 7 to each corresponding fiber, giving 29 or 21. The attached independent RREF and triple enumerators both recover all 1395 spaces and the same 63 fibers. Direct field operations check the determinant identity and all 651 common-two-space incidence constraints. No extrapolation beyond \(n=6\) is asserted.

originality.rationale: The exact 63-fiber distribution, the nine norm-one high fibers, and the 4/3 scalar-orbit allocation are not present in or implied by the strongest inspected primary texts. The 2025 construction establishes only a proper determinant coloring; the 2026 sum-free paper identifies the same witness mechanism and a different 31-coloring, without determining this specific 63-coloring spectrum. The determinant identity and the 63-color upper bound are acknowledged as old. Public research-record and literature alias/parameter searches found no record asserting the new spectrum; non-indexed prior computation remains a risk.
residual_risks: A specialized finite-geometry database or unindexed prior computation could already contain the same 63 determinant fiber counts.
The result is restricted to the fixed 63-color Moore construction; no new chromatic bound is obtained and the separate 31-color construction is stronger for that purpose.

value.rationale: The complete class-size spectrum of a canonical Grassmannian/constant-dimension code partition is a natural invariant for assessing its balance and fiber geometry. Unlike a mere reproduction of the already known 63-color bound, the result isolates an exact nine-class norm-one excess explained by the unique subfield orbit and fully classifies all 23 scalar orbits. It addresses a mathematically natural finite self-dual case (three-spaces in a six-space), not an arbitrary parameter slice, and makes no unsupported claim to improve the known 31-color construction.
